questions.title: Assembly program trace
questions.text:
Assembly language mnemonics

| Mnemonic | Meaning |
|---|---|
| INP | Retrieve user input and stores it in the Accumulator. |
| OUT | Output the value stored in the Accumulator. |
| LDA | Load the Accumulator with the contents of the memory address given. |
| STA | Store the value in the Accumulator in the memory address given. |
| ADD | Add the contents of the memory address to the Accumulator. |
| SUB | Subtract the contents of the memory address from the Accumulator. |
| BRP | Branch/Jump to the address given if the Accumulator is zero or positive. |
| BRZ | Jump to the address given in case the Accumulator is zero. |
| BRA | Jump to the address given. |
| HLT | Stop the code. |
| DAT | Used to associate a label to a free memory address. An optional value can also be used to be stored at the memory address. |

Analyse the program below.

| Line number | Address | Instruction |
|---:|---:|---|
| 1 | 00 | LDA 08 |
| 2 | 01 | SUB 09 |
| 3 | 02 | BRP 06 |
| 4 | 03 | LDA 08 |
| 5 | 04 | OUT |
| 6 | 05 | HLT |
| 7 | 06 | STA 08 |
| 8 | 07 | BRA 00 |
| 9 | 08 | DAT 6 |
| 10 | 09 | DAT 4 |

questions.text:
The array PhoneBook stores 100 names in alphabetical order.

The binary search algorithm is used to find a name.

parts.title: Binary search (a)
parts.text:
Complete the pseudocode.

```pseudocode
1   INPUT name
2   low ← 0
3   index ← -1
4   high ← LENGTH(PhoneBook) - 1
5   flag ← FALSE
6   WHILE( ……………………………… OR flag<>TRUE)
7       mid ← INT((low+high)/2)
8       IF ……………………………………………………………
9           ……………………………………………………………
10          ……………………………………………………………
11      ELSE IF PhoneBook[mid]>name THEN
12            ……………………………………………………………
13            ELSE
14               low ← mid+1
15            ENDIF
16      ENDIF
17  ENDWHILE
18  IF ………………………………………………………………………… THEN
19      OUTPUT(“The name is found at index:”,index)
20  ELSE
21      OUTPUT(“The name does not exist in array”)
    ENDIF
```

Note: `INT()` return integer part of a number.
`LENGTH()` return size of an array.

questions.title: Stack operations
questions.text:
A stack is an abstract data type that holds an ordered linear sequence of items.

The main stack operations are:

| Operation | Description |
|---|---|
| push(data) | adds an element to the top of the stack |
| pop() | removes an element from the top of the stack |
| peek() | returns a copy of the element on the top of the stack without removing it |
| is_empty() | checks whether a stack is empty |
| is_full() | checks whether a stack is at maximum capacity when stored in a static (fixed-size) structure |

State A stack, bottom to top: Java, Python, Kotlin. Pointer points to the top item Kotlin.

State B stack, bottom to top: Java, C#, C++.

Write down a list of stack operations to get stack from State A to State B.

parts.title: Caesar cipher web application (c)(i)
parts.text:
The pseudocode for a function is given below.

```pseudocode
FUNCTION Encrypt(text)
1       // Size of array fixed.
        alphabet ← ['a', 'b', 'c', 'd', 'e', 'f', 'g',
        'h', 'i', 'j', 'k', 'l', 'm', 'n', 'o', 'p',
        'q', 'r', 's', 't', 'u', 'v', 'w', 'x', 'y',
2       'z']
3       result ← ""
4       text ← text.lower()
5       FOR i ← 0 TO length(text)-1 DO
6            FOR j ← 0 TO length(alphabet)-1 DO
7                IF text[i]= alphabet[j] THEN
8                     result ← result + alphabet[j+1]
9                ENDIF
10           ENDFOR
11      ENDFOR
12      RETURN result
13  ENDFUNCTION
```

Note:
`lower()` – takes no arguments and returns the lowercase strings from the given string by converting each uppercase character to lowercase.
For example:
`"Apple".lower()="apple"`

Provide one example of normal data for the algorithm.
